mainTopic: When does a handle (יד) or protection (שומר) count with a small amount of food for טומאה, and is a bean's size a real minimum?
overview: This amud deals with when an attached part of food, a יד (handle) or a שומר (protection, like a shell or bone), counts together with the food for טומאה, and how much food it needs. The גמרא tests רב and רבי יוחנן against two ברייתות about bones with a little meat on them. Each time, רב survives by agreeing with one of the two תנאים, depending on whether the bone is read as a handle or a protection. רבי יוחנן reads the thigh-bone ברייתא as all about protection and follows אחרים. Their 'bean's size' is explained as just matching the wording of the תנא קמא, and רבא shows from the word קולית that the case is about protection. Next comes a dispute: רבי חנינא says the bean's size is a real minimum for a שומר, while רבי יוחנן says it is not. Two challenges to the minimum are answered. The pod case of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is about the stalk acting as a handle, and single grains in their shells are different because each grain is a whole item (בריה). The amud ends as רב אושעיא opens a new question, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How does רב explain the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב. Whether the bone in the ברייתא is a handle or a protection, one clause of the ברייתא seems to argue with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רב explain this ברייתא? If it is talking about a handle, the first clause is a problem. If it is talking about a protection, the last clause is a problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב can fit the ברייתא with his own rules. It shows that both ways of reading the case cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bone is a יד, the תנא קמא makes the house impure even though the flesh is less than a כזית. That goes against רב, who says such a handle does not count. If the bone is a שומר, רבי יהודה בן נקוסא keeps the house pure. That goes against רב, who says a שומר counts as long as the flesh is at least a כפול.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets it up, meaning explains which case the source is talking about
A handle: an attached part that you hold the food by
A protection: an attached part that guards the food, like a shell or peel
The first clause of a source
The last clause of a source
It is difficult; a problem

steps.confusionAlert: The two problems come from two different clauses. The handle reading clashes with the first opinion, the תנא קמא. The protection reading clashes with the second opinion, רבי יהודה בן נקוסא.

phrases.english: And Rav, how does he explain this [baraita]?
phrases.notes: "This" means the ברייתא about a bone with less than a כזית of flesh on it.

phrases.english: If [it is talking] about a handle,
the first clause is difficult!
phrases.notes: The first opinion makes the house impure, but רב says a handle on less than a כזית doesn't count.

phrases.english: If [it is talking] about a protection,
the last clause is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא quoted just before this passage to challenge רב's rules on יד and שומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rules for when a יד or a שומר counts for passing on טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: either reading of the bone leaves one clause of the ברייתא arguing with רב.

steps.title: Either reading can work for רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב can read the ברייתא as talking about a protection or as talking about a handle.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is talking about a protection. If you want, say it is talking about a handle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short answer: both readings work for רב. It explains how in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not pick one side of the dilemma. It says either side is fine. That suggests the problem is solved by having רב agree with just one תנא, not with the whole ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: it opens one of two possible answers

phrases.english: If you wish, say [it is talking] about a protection,
if you wish, say [it is talking] about a handle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא בְּשׁוֹמֵר, אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא בְּיָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma from step 1 by accepting both readings.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two possible answers: either reading of the case works
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both readings fail, because each one clashes with one clause of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each reading is fine. Step 3 explains why.

steps.title: רב agrees with one תנא in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: If the bone is a handle, רב follows רבי יהודה בן נקוסא. If the bone is a protection, רב follows the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is talking about a handle, and רב holds like רבי יהודה בן נקוסא. Or if you want, say it is talking about a protection, and רב holds like the תנא קמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains its two answers. In each reading, רב agrees with the תנא whose view matches his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the handle reading, רבי יהודה בן נקוסא keeps the house pure, just as רב says a handle on less than a כזית doesn't count. In the protection reading, the תנא קמא makes the house impure, just as רב says a protection counts if the flesh is at least a כפול. A problem from the other clause doesn't matter, because רב is allowed to follow one side of a מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: And he said his view in line with a certain תנא
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

steps.whatToRemember: רב's rules are not disproved by this ברייתא. Whichever way you read the bone, רב is simply agreeing with one of the two תנאים in it: רבי יהודה בן נקוסא if it is a handle, or the תנא קמא if it is a protection.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא. When an אמורא seems to clash with a source that has a מחלוקת, the answer can be that he follows the other side of that מחלוקת.

phrases.english: If you wish, say [it is talking] about a handle,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן נָקוֹסָא,
phrases.english: and he [Rav] said his view in line with Rabbi Yehuda ben Nekosa,
and if you wish, say [it is talking] about a protection,
and he [Rav] said his view in line with the first tanna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא בְּיָד, וְהוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן נָקוֹסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the two answers from step 2 in order to explain them, adding which תנא רב follows in each.
steps.terutzResolutionType: רב follows one side of a מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב has to fit both clauses of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows רבי יהודה בן נקוסא if the bone is a handle, and the תנא קמא if it is a protection.

steps.title: How רבי יוחנן reads the earlier ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן can say the whole ברייתא is about a handle, and he follows the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן can say: the whole ברייתא is talking about a handle, and he holds like the first תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after answering for רב, the גמרא now shows how רבי יוחנן can also fit the earlier ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that a handle attached to less than a כזית of food does bring impurity. So he reads the whole ברייתא as being about a handle. He sides with the תנא קמא, who says it is impure, and not with רבי יהודה בן נקוסא.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, meaning the whole ברייתא
A handle, a part attached to food that you can hold it by
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
phrases.notes: He means רבי יוחנן could answer this way. He isn't quoted saying it.

phrases.english: The whole of it is about a handle,
and he stated his view like the first tanna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's answer to the same challenge that steps 2–3 answered for רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the source a certain way and siding with one of its opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to argue with רבי יוחנן too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read as being about a handle, the תנא קמא agrees with רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: A new source about a thigh bone with meat on it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says a thigh bone needs a כזית of meat on it to draw the whole bone into impurity, while אחרים say even a bean's size is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says, a thigh bone with a כזית of meat on it draws all of it into impurity. אחרים say: even if there is only a bean's size of meat on it, it draws all of it into impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing a new source. It is setting up a fresh challenge to רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a thigh bone with meat on it that touches impurity. רבי יהודה says the meat pulls the whole bone into impurity only if there is a כזית. אחרים say even a bean's size, which is less than a כזית, is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A thigh bone (femur)
The size of an olive, the usual minimum amount for food impurity
Drags into impurity: makes the attached part count as part of the food for impurity
The size of a bean, smaller than a כזית

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Yehuda says,
a thigh bone that has an olive-bulk of meat on it –
draws the whole of it into impurity.
phrases.notes: The meat pulls the whole bone in, so touching any part of the bone makes it impure.

phrases.english: Others say:
even if there is only a bean-bulk on it –
it draws the whole of it into impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge using a different ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: you need a כזית of meat for the bone to be included. אחרים: even a bean's size is enough.

steps.title: Either way, this source seems to argue with רב
steps.stepSummary: If the bone is a handle, the second clause argues with רב. If it is a protection, the first clause argues with רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does רב explain this ברייתא? If it is about a handle, the end is hard. If it is about a protection, the beginning is hard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב can fit this ברייתא, since each way of reading it clashes with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that a handle with less than a כזית does not bring impurity, but a protection with less than a כזית does. If the bone is a handle, אחרים say a bean's size is enough, which goes against רב. If the bone is a protection, רבי יהודה requires a full כזית, which also goes against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains or sets up a source as talking about a certain case
A protection, a part that guards the food, like a shell or peel
The end clause of a source
The first clause of a source

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two halves. A 'handle' reading clashes with the second opinion (אחרים). A 'protection' reading clashes with the first opinion (רבי יהודה).

phrases.english: And Rav, in what way does he explain this?
If it is about a handle – the end clause is difficult,
if it is about a protection – the first clause is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 5 to challenge רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view: a handle with less than a כזית is not impure, but a protection with less than a כזית is.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided trap: each reading of the bone makes one clause of the ברייתא argue with רב.

steps.title: רב simply follows one of the two opinions
steps.stepSummary: If the bone is a handle, רב follows רבי יהודה. If it is a protection, רב follows אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is about a handle, and רב holds like רבי יהודה. Or if you want, say it is about a protection, and רב holds like אחרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב is allowed to side with one of the two opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An argument between תנאים doesn't disprove רב. He just picks one side. Read as a handle, רבי יהודה agrees that less than a כזית is not impure. Read as a protection, אחרים agree that less than a כזית is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: it introduces one of two possible answers

steps.whatToRemember: Just like with the first ברייתא, רב survives by siding with one opinion. Handle means he follows רבי יהודה. Protection means he follows אחרים.

phrases.english: If you wish, say it is about a handle –
and he stated his view like Rabbi Yehuda,
and if you wish, say it is about a protection – like Others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Siding with one opinion in an argument between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Whichever way we read the bone, the ברייתא seemed to argue with רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows רבי יהודה if the bone is a handle, or אחרים if it is a protection.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן reads the whole ברייתא as protection and follows אחרים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן can say the whole ברייתא is about a protecting bone (שומר), and he follows אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן says: the whole ברייתא is about a protecting bone, and he holds like אחרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יוחנן can fit this new ברייתא. He says it is all about a bone that protects, and he sides with אחרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the גמרא needed two readings: handle or protection. רבי יוחנן reads the whole ברייתא one way, as protection. אחרים give the smallest amount of meat, so he lines up with them.

keyTerms.meaning: all of it, the whole ברייתא
a protecting part, like a bone or shell that guards food and joins it for טומאה
'others', a group of תנאים named this way in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
the whole of it is about protection,
phrases.notes: He means the whole ברייתא from Step 5, both רבי יהודה's part and אחרים's part.

phrases.english: and he holds like Aḥerim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels Step 7. After fitting רב into the ברייתא, the גמרא now fits רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the whole source as one case and siding with one of its opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא might seem to go against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is all about שומר, and רבי יוחנן follows אחרים.

steps.title: But אחרים still say a bean's size
steps.stepSummary: אחרים do give a minimum, a bean's size, so how can רבי יוחנן, who allows less, follow them?
steps.simpleTranslation: But אחרים say 'a bean's size'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. אחרים set a minimum of a bean's size, so they do not fully match רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that a protecting bone joins meat even if there is less than a bean's size. אחרים clearly name a bean's size as the amount needed. So agreeing with אחרים does not seem to work.

keyTerms.meaning: the size of a bean, a small measure of food

phrases.english: Aḥerim,
but they say 'a bean-bulk'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 8's claim that רבי יוחנן follows אחרים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 8 that רבי יוחנן holds like אחרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אחרים require a bean's size, while רבי יוחנן allows less. So their views do not match.

steps.title: אחרים named a size only to match the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: אחרים really agree that even less counts. They named a bean's size only because the תנא קמא named a size.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the תנא קמא said a measure, they also said a measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The words 'a bean's size' are not a real minimum for אחרים. They are only a style of speaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא (רבי יהודה) said a כזית, so אחרים answered back with a size too. Really they hold that even less than a bean's size joins. So רבי יוחנן can follow them after all.

keyTerms.meaning: since, because (the wording follows the other side's wording)
the first opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
a set measure or amount

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אחרים truly require a bean's size. According to this answer, the bean's size is just how they phrased it, not a real minimum.

phrases.english: since the first tanna states a measure,
phrases.notes: The תנא קמא here is רבי יהודה, who said a כזית.

phrases.english: they also state a measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The wording only matches the other opinion's wording (איידי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אחרים set a real minimum of a bean's size.
steps.terutzMaskana: אחרים hold that even less counts. They named a size only to match the תנא קמא, so רבי יוחנן fits them.

steps.title: רבא: the word 'thigh bone' shows it is about protection
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports the reading that the ברייתא is about שומר, because it picks a thigh bone (קולית).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the wording also shows we are dealing with protection, since it says 'thigh bone'. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings support from the exact wording of the ברייתא. Its choice of a thigh bone shows that it is talking about a protecting bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thigh bone has marrow inside, so the bone guards the food in it. If the ברייתא were about a handle, any bone with meat would do. Picking a thigh bone points to protection, which backs up רבי יוחנן's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: the exact wording also shows this
thigh bone, which has marrow inside
learn from this, this is proven

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן reads the whole ברייתא as about a protecting bone (שומר) and follows אחרים. Their 'bean's size' is only wording. רבא supports this from the word קולית, a marrow bone that protects what is inside.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives רבי יוחנן's reading support from the text itself, not just a way to make it possible.

phrases.english: Rava said:
it is also precise,
phrases.notes: He means the exact words of the ברייתא support this.

phrases.english: that we are dealing with protection,
since it teaches 'a femur',
phrases.notes: A thigh bone has marrow inside, so the bone guards it.

phrases.english: conclude from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי דִּבְשׁוֹמֵר עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge is answered, רבא adds proof from the wording that the ברייתא is about שומר, as in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא about the thigh bone is talking about שומר, not a handle.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's choice of the word קולית, a bone with marrow inside.

steps.title: A dispute over whether the bean's size is a real minimum
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא holds that the bean's size of אחרים is a real minimum. רבי יוחנן holds that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי חנינא says, this is a real measure. And רבי יוחנן says, this is not a real measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an official dispute about the 'bean's size' that אחרים mentioned in the ברייתא. Is it a true minimum, or not?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי חנינא, a protecting part (שומר) only passes on טומאה if at least a bean's size of food is attached to it. According to רבי יוחנן, אחרים agree that even less food is enough. This matches what the earlier steps said about רבי יוחנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A set minimum amount required for a הלכה to apply
'This is a measure', meaning the number given is a true minimum
'This is not a measure', meaning the number given is not a true minimum

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute is the source of everything that follows in this part. Each side of it will now be tested.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: זֶהוּ שִׁיעוּר,
phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Ḥanina says: This is a measure,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the bean's size that אחרים gave in the ברייתא about the thigh bone.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֵין זֶה שִׁיעוּר.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yoḥanan says: This is not a measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: זֶהוּ שִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally records, as an open dispute, the question about the bean's size that steps 9 and 10 raised for רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא: a bean's size is the minimum for a שומר. רבי יוחנן: no minimum, so even less counts.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי יוחנן from the words 'like a bean'
steps.stepSummary: How can רבי יוחנן say there is no minimum, when the ברייתא says 'a bean's size'?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This is not a measure'? But the ברייתא clearly teaches 'like a bean'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן from the plain wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחרים explicitly said 'כפול', a bean's size. That sounds like a minimum, which goes against רבי יוחנן's claim that even less counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a bean, meaning the size of a bean
'But surely…', used to open a challenge

phrases.english: This is not a measure?
But doesn't it teach 'like a bean'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's side of the dispute in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the bean's size is not a minimum
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's explicit wording 'כפול' seems to set a minimum.

steps.title: אחרים named a size only because the תנא קמא did
steps.stepSummary: The bean's size is not a real minimum. It was said only to match the style of the תנא קמא, who gave a size.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the תנא קמא said a measure, they (אחרים) also said a measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. The words 'like a bean' were said only to answer in the same style as the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא gave a set size (an olive's size), so אחרים answered with a size too. That does not mean they really require that much. The same answer was already given in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since…', used when something is said only because of the wording of something else
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
Also

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אחרים are making the rule stricter than רבי יוחנן says. On this reading, 'like a bean' is just an echo of the תנא קמא's style, not a real requirement.

phrases.english: Since the first tanna stated a measure,
they too stated a measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording as copying the style of the first opinion
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כפול' only mirrors the תנא קמא's style. אחרים agree that even less counts.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's ruling on pods
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה makes a pod of small legumes impure even with tiny amounts of food. This seems to go against requiring a bean's size.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה rules a pod of beans pure, and rules a pod of small legumes impure, because a person wants the pod when handling them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems to go against רב (and רבי חנינא), who require a minimum amount of food for a שומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pod of big beans is not needed for protection, so it is pure. A pod of small legumes is wanted for handling them, so it is impure. Since each tiny grain is less than a bean's size, it looks like a שומר passes on טומאה even with less than a bean's size.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules it ritually pure
Rules it ritually impure
Small legumes, like lentils
Handling or using something

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya

phrases.aramaic: מְטַהֵר בְּשֶׁל פּוֹל, וּמְטַמֵּא בְּשֶׁל קִטְנִית,
phrases.english: rules pure in the case of a bean pod, and rules impure in the case of a legume pod,
phrases.notes: He is talking about a pod that touched a dead שרץ.

phrases.english: because one wants it when handling them!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה מְטַהֵר בְּשֶׁל פּוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending רבי יוחנן to challenging the side that requires a minimum (רב and רבי חנינא).
steps.kashyaTarget: רב (and רבי חנינא), who require a minimum amount of food for a שומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A legume pod becomes impure because of tiny grains of less than a bean's size, so a שומר seems to work with no minimum.

steps.title: The pod case is about the stalk as a handle
steps.stepSummary: Following רב אחא בריה דרבא, the שרץ touched the stalk, and the ruling is about a handle (יד), not a protecting part (שומר).
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב אחא son of רבא said: it is a case of the stalk, and it is because of the rules of a handle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting an explanation רב אחא בריה דרבא gave for this משנה in another discussion: the case is about the stalk acting as a handle. The next step applies this to our challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שרץ touched the stalk, the stalk passes on טומאה as a handle (יד), not as a protection (שומר). So the case does not show that a שומר works with less than a bean's size. Step 17 explains why the handle rule fits too: one stalk holds many pods.

keyTerms.meaning: The stalk that the pod grows on
A handle, a part used to hold food, which can pass on טומאה
Because of, under the rules of

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא and רב require a bean's size for a שומר, while רבי יוחנן requires no minimum. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's pod case does not disprove the minimum, because it is about the stalk as a handle (יד), not about protection.

phrases.english: As Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said,
in the case of the stalk, and because of a handle.
phrases.notes: He means the שרץ touched the stalk, not the pod itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: it is about a handle, not protection
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pod is a שומר that passes on טומאה with less than a bean's size.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שרץ touched the stalk, which works as a handle (יד). So the case says nothing about the minimum for a שומר.

steps.title: The pod case is about the stalk acting as a handle
steps.stepSummary: Using the approach of רב אחא בריה דרבא, the גמרא says the משנה of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is about a שרץ touching the stalk, which counts as a handle (יד). It reads the word במשמושן as בתשמישן, meaning 'using them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the case is about the stalk, and the rule comes from the laws of a handle. And what does 'when handling them' mean? It means 'when using them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the answer of רב אחא בריה דרבא to the משנה of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, so that it no longer goes against רבי חנינא. It also explains one word in that משנה so it fits this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that tiny legumes in their pod become impure, which seems to ignore the bean's size minimum. The answer: the שרץ touched the stalk, and one stalk holds many pods, so it is a handle for more than the minimum amount of food. The word במשמושן is read as בתשמישן, 'using them', meaning people carry the legumes by the stalk.

keyTerms.meaning: The stalk, which holds many pods together
A handle: a part used to hold or carry the food
'When handling them', the word used in the משנה
'When using them', meaning carrying the legumes by the stalk

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up יד (a handle you hold the food by) with שומר (a part that protects the food, like a shell). The answer works because the case is moved from שומר to יד.

phrases.english: Here too, it is about the stalk,
phrases.notes: 'Here too' means we use the same answer רב אחא בריה דרבא gave before, now for the pod case.

phrases.english: and the rule is because of a handle.
And what does 'when handling them' mean?
When using them.
phrases.notes: He means people use the stalk to carry the legumes, which is exactly what a handle does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from Step 16 by applying it to the pod case and explaining one word in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (stalk and handle, not shell and protection) plus rereading a word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pod protects tiny legumes, so a שומר would work even with less than a bean's size.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is about the stalk as a handle for many pods together, so it does not go against the bean's size minimum.
steps.whatToRemember: The pod case is about the stalk as a handle (יד), not about protection (שומר). So it does not disprove רבי חנינא.

steps.title: Challenge from grains kept in their shells
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns from a פסוק that wheat, barley and lentils are impure together with their shells. Each grain is smaller than a bean, so this seems to go against the bean's size minimum.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'On any sowing seed that is sown.' This means the seed in the form people take it out to sow: wheat in its shell, barley in its shell, and lentils in their shells!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to challenge רבי חנינא. Here the shell protects a tiny grain, much smaller than a bean, and it still counts together with the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about seed in the form people sow it, and people sow grain in its shell. So the shell counts as part of the food for impurity. A single grain is far smaller than a bean, so this suggests a שומר works even without a bean's size.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Sowing seed', the words of the פסוק about food impurity
Shell or husk around the grain
A protecting part of food, like a shell, that counts together with the food
A teaching from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"On any sowing seed that is sown":
in the way that people take it out to sow,
wheat in its shell,
and barley in its shell,
and lentils in their shells!
phrases.notes: Each grain or lentil is much smaller than a bean, and that is the whole point of the challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the pod challenge was answered, the גמרא brings another source against the bean's size minimum.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי חנינא (and רב) that a שומר needs at least a bean's size of food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A shell counts together with a single grain, which is less than a bean's size, so the minimum seems not to apply.

steps.title: A whole separate item is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a single grain is a בריה, a complete item of its own, so it has a special rule. Its shell counts even though it is smaller than a bean.
steps.simpleTranslation: A whole, separate item is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the challenge from the grains. It says grains are a special case, so they teach nothing about other food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A grain of wheat or a lentil is a complete natural item, not a piece cut from something bigger. For such a whole item, the shell counts with it even below a bean's size. The general minimum of רבי חנינא still applies to ordinary food.

keyTerms.meaning: A whole, complete item of its own, like a single grain
Is different, has its own rule

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the bean's size minimum is a general rule, but a whole separate item like a grain is an exception.

phrases.english: A whole, separate item is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18 by making grains a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception: a whole separate item has its own rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Grains in shells prove a שומר works even with less than a bean's size, for all food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a whole item like a grain is different; the bean's size minimum still holds for other food.
steps.whatToRemember: The bean's size minimum stays in place. Single grains in their shells are an exception because each grain is a whole item (בריה).

steps.title: רב אושעיא opens a new question
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא is about to ask an unresolved question. This line only introduces it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא asked a question:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: a new question from רב אושעיא. The question itself comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בעי means a real question that is not yet decided, not an attack on someone. The topic of the question has not been stated yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks a question that has no clear answer yet

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya asked a question:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenges to רבי חנינא are answered, the גמרא moves on to a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Not stated yet; the question comes after this opening line.
